full: Darar bin al-Khattab b. Murdas b. Kabir(Kathir) b. 'Amr b. Habib b. 'Amr b. Shiban b. Muharib b.Fihr

bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 4193, continuing on page 1624) cites Ibn Hibban for his companionship and describes him as a horseman and poet, said to be the best poet of Quraysh after Ibn al-Ziba'ra. It quotes Ibn Sa'd that he is mentioned at Uhud and al-Khandaq, became Muslim at the conquest of Mecca, and was killed as a martyr at al-Yamama, while al-Khatib reports he lived on to witness the conquest of al-Mada'in and settled in Syria. Ibn Manda notes he has no transmitted hadith; no death year is given.

She is the one who sent the Prophet a gift of clarified butter, dried curd and a dabb (lizard), a report transmitted via Sulayman ibn Yasar and others from Maymuna and found in both Sahih collections; the Prophet did not eat the lizard. No death year is given.

bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 11676) identifies her as the paternal aunt of al-Ash'ath ibn Qays and the mother of the Companion Mu'awiya ibn Hudayj. It reports that she vowed to circumambulate the Ka'ba crawling, and the Prophet told her to walk instead.
research_evidence: كبشة بنت معديكرب: عمة الأشعث بن قيس، وهي والدة معاوية بن حديج الصحابي
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full: Saif ibn Qays b. Ma'di-Karib b. Mau'wiya b. Jabla b. 'Aidy b. Rabi'a al-Kundi
full_name_ar: سيف بن قيس بن معدي كرب ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 3647) identifies him as the brother of al-Ash'ath ibn Qays, mentioned by Ibn Shahin. It cites al-Kalbi that when Sayf came to the Prophet he was ordered to give the call to prayer (adhan) for his people and continued doing so until he died; Abu 'Umar (Ibn 'Abd al-Barr) affirmed his companionship and al-Baghawi reported a similar account.
research_evidence: سيف بن قيس بن معديكرب، أخو الأشعث بن قيس. ذكره ابن شاهين، وساق إلى الكلبيّ
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full: Qays bin Makshuh (Hubayra) bin Abd Yaghuth b. al-Guzayl b. Salma b. Bada b. 'Amir of Murad or Bajli
full_name_ar: قيس بن المكشوح المرادي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 7254) identifies him as Qays ibn al-Makshuh al-Muradi and quotes Ibn 'Abd al-Barr that his companionship is disputed: some deny it, others affirm he met and saw the Prophet. The entry reports he accepted Islam in the time of Abu Bakr or 'Umar and took part in the conquest of Nahawand.
research_evidence: قيس بن المكشوح: المرادي. يأتي في القسم الثاني، قال ابن عبد البرّ: قيل: لا صحبة له. وقيل: بل له صحبة باللقاء والرؤية
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full: Umm Muslim al-Ashja'iyya
full_name_ar: أم مسلم الأشجعية ( رضي الله عنها
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 12255) says she had companionship and that her hadith is found among the people of Kufa, transmitted by al-Thawri, citing Abu 'Umar (Ibn 'Abd al-Barr). It notes Ibn al-Sakan recorded her report via al-Thawri with Habib ibn Abi Thabit in the chain; footnotes refer to Usd al-Ghaba and al-Isti'ab.
research_evidence: ١٢٢٥٥- أم مسلم الأشجعية: لها صحبة، حديثها عند أهل الكوفة، رواه الثوري، قاله أبو عمر
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full: Abu Muwaihibah, Ahmar, Clinet of Prophet (saw)
full_name_ar: أبو مويهبة مولى رسول الله صلى الله عليه ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 10595) lists him as a client of the Prophet, also called Abu Mawhiba. It quotes al-Baladhuri that he was born among Muzayna, took part in the raid of al-Muraysi' and led 'A'isha's camel. His hadith about the Prophet visiting al-Baqi' cemetery before his death is recorded by Ahmad, al-Darimi and others, with 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As narrating from him.
research_evidence: أبو مويهبة: ويقال أبو موهبة، وأبو موهوبة، وهو قول الواقدي: مولى رسول اللَّه صلى اللَّه عليه وسلّم. قال البلاذريّ: كان من مولدي مزينة
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full: Zayd bin Bola, Clinet of Prophet (saw)
full_name_ar: زيد مولى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 2886) identifies him as Zayd ibn Bula, client of the Prophet, with the kunya Abu Yasar, who has a hadith in Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi transmitted through his grandson Bilal ibn Yasar ibn Zayd from his father. It quotes Ibn Shahin that he was Nubian, captured by the Prophet on the expedition against Banu Tha'laba and then freed.
research_evidence: ٢٨٨٦ ز- زيد بن بولا: بالموحدة، مولى رسول اللَّه صلّى اللَّه عليه وسلّم، أبو يسار. له حديث عند أبي داود، والترمذيّ
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full: 'Ubaid, Clinet of Prophet (saw)
full_name_ar: عبيد مولى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 5385) quotes Ibn Hibban that he had companionship and Ibn al-Sakan that his hadith is not established; al-Baladhuri says he narrated two hadiths. Ahmad ibn Hanbal transmits them via Sulayman al-Taymi: one on prayer between Maghrib and 'Isha, the other on two fasting women who backbit. Ibn 'Abd al-Barr notes Sulayman did not hear directly from him.
research_evidence: وقال البلاذريّ: يقال إنه كان لرسول اللَّه صلى اللَّه عليه وسلّم مولى يقال له عبيد، روى عنه حديثين
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full: Waqid, Clinet of Prophet (saw)
full_name_ar: واقد مولى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 9118) lists him as a client of the Prophet, mentioned by al-Hasan ibn Sufyan in his Musnad and al-Tabarani in his Mu'jam. Both transmit via Zadhan from Waqid the hadith that whoever obeys God has remembered God even if his prayer and fasting are few.
research_evidence: واقد: مولى رسول اللَّه صلّى اللَّه عليه وآله وسلّم. ذكره الحسن بن سفيان في مسندة، والطّبرانيّ في معجمه

full: Mad'um the Black, Clinet of Prophet (saw)
full_name_ar: مدعم الأسود مولى رسول الله صلى الله عليه ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 7873) says he was a client of the Prophet, born at Hisma, and given to the Prophet by Rifa'a ibn Zayd al-Judhami. His mention is established in the Muwatta' and the two Sahihs via Abu Hurayra's account of the conquest of Khaybar, where he was killed by a stray arrow. Al-Baladhuri reports he was said to have the kunya Abu Sallam, and that some say he was given by Farwa ibn 'Amr al-Judhami.
research_evidence: مدعم الأسود: مولى رسول اللَّه صلّى اللَّه عليه وآله وسلّم. كان مولدا من حسمى، أهداه رفاعة بن زيد الجذاميّ لرسول اللَّه
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full: Nauba the Black, Clinet of Prophet (saw)
full_name_ar: نوبة الأسود مولى رسول الله ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 8846) lists him as a client of the Prophet. It quotes Sayf ibn 'Umar's Kitab al-Ridda wa al-Futuh with a report from 'A'isha that during the Prophet's final illness a black slave called Nauba and Barira supported him between them to the mosque while Abu Bakr was leading the prayer.
research_evidence: ٨٨٤٦- نوبة الأسود: مولى رسول اللَّه صلّى اللَّه عليه وآله وسلّم
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full: Rabah the Black, Clinet of Prophet (saw)
full_name_ar: رباح مولى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba lists Rabah as a client of the Prophet whose mention is established in the two Sahihs through 'Umar's account. It quotes al-Baladhuri that he was black and served as the Prophet's doorkeeper, and that after the death of Yasar he was put in charge of the Prophet's livestock.
research_evidence: رباح: مولى رسول اللَّه صلّى اللَّه عليه وآله وسلم. ثبت ذكره في الصحيحين من حديث عمر في قصة
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full: Kirkirah, Clinet of Prophet (saw)
full_name_ar: كركرة مولى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 7415, كركرة) describes him as a Nubian client of the Prophet who was given to him by Hawdha ibn 'Ali al-Hanafi al-Yamami, and the Prophet freed him. The entry's footnote refers to Usd al-Ghaba.
research_evidence: مولى رسول اللَّه صلّى اللَّه عليه وآله وسلم، كان نوبيّا أهداه له هوذة بن علي الحنفي اليمامي فأعتقه
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full: Fadala, Clinet of Prophet (saw)
full_name_ar: فضالة مولى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 7014) describes him as a client of the Prophet from Yemen. Ja'far al-Mustaghfiri reported he settled in al-Sham; Abu Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn Hazm and Abu 'Umar (Ibn 'Abd al-Barr) listed him among the Prophet's clients, and Ibn Sa'd, citing al-Waqidi, said he settled in al-Sham where his children were born.
research_evidence: فضالة: مولى رسول اللَّه صلّى اللَّه عليه وآله وسلم: من أهل اليمن. نقل جعفر المستغفريّ أنه نزل الشام

full: Nafi', Clinet of Prophet (saw)
full_name_ar: نافع مولى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 8689) lists him as a client of the Prophet and quotes Ibn Abi Hatim from his father that he had companionship. It cites a chain through Yazid ibn Harun and Yusuf ibn Maymun from Nafi' with the hadith 'No adulterous old man, arrogant person, or one who reminds God of his deeds will enter Paradise', and a report that the Prophet told him hardship would afflict him after his death.
research_evidence: ٨٦٨٩- نافع: مولى رسول اللَّه صلى اللَّه عليه وآله وسلم

full: Abu 'Ubaid, Clinet of Prophet (saw)
full_name_ar: أبو عبيد مولى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 10230) lists him as a client of the Prophet whose name is unknown, as noted by al-Hakim Abu Ahmad. Al-Tirmidhi (in al-Shama'il) and al-Darimi record his hadith via Shahr ibn Hawshab, in which he cooked a pot for the Prophet, who liked the foreleg. Al-Baghawi affirmed his companionship.
research_evidence: أبو عبيد: مولى رسول اللَّه صلى اللَّه عليه وسلّم ذكره الحاكم أبو أحمد فيمن لا يعرف اسمه وأخرج حديثه الترمذي في الشمائل والدّارميّ من طريق شهر بن حوشب عنه
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full: Hisham, Clinet of Prophet (saw)
full_name_ar: هشام مولى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 8996, continuing on the next page) lists him as a client of the Prophet. It cites a hadith he transmitted via al-Thawri, 'Abd al-Karim al-Jazari and Abu al-Zubayr about a man who asked the Prophet about his wife, reported by al-Tabarani, Ibn Qani' and Ibn Manda. Abu 'Umar (Ibn 'Abd al-Barr) noted that some identified Hisham himself as the questioner; footnotes point to Usd al-Ghaba and al-Isti'ab.
research_evidence: ٨٩٩٦- هشام، مولى رسول اللَّه صلّى اللَّه عليه وآله وسلّم

full: Abu Dumairah al-Humayri, Clinet of Prophet (saw)
full_name_ar: أبو ضميرة الحميري ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 10160) says Ibn Manda, al-Baghawi and Ibn Sa'd described him as a client of the Prophet; his personal name is disputed (Sa'd or Ruh are suggested). The entry refers to a letter the Prophet wrote for the family of Dumayra, which his descendant Husayn ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Dumayra later presented to the caliph al-Mahdi.
research_evidence: أبو ضميرة الحميري والد ضميرة: ذكره ابن مندة في الكنى، وسبقه البغويّ ومن قبله محمد بن سعد، ووصفوه بأنه مولى رسول اللَّه صلى اللَّه عليه وسلّم
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full: Abu Waqid, Clinet of Prophet (saw)
full_name_ar: أبو واقد مولى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 10702) lists him as a client of the Prophet, citing Ibn Manda that Zadhan ibn 'Umar narrated from him. The hadith, via al-Haytham ibn Jimaz, says whoever obeys God has remembered God even if his prayer, fasting and recitation are few. The editor's notes cite al-Haythami, who called al-Haytham ibn Jimaz abandoned (matruk).
research_evidence: أبو واقد، مولى النبي صلى اللَّه عليه وسلّم. ذكره ابن مندة، فقال: روى عنه زاذان بن عمر
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full: Sundar, Clinet of Prophet (saw)
full_name_ar: سندر مولى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 3530, continuing on the next page) identifies him as the client of Zinba' al-Judhami whom the Prophet freed, and quotes al-Bukhari that he had companionship. It cites al-Tabarani and Ibn Manda for a report that he asked 'Umar ibn al-Khattab to register his stipend in Egypt, where he settled. The entry gives his kunya as Abu al-Aswad and says he lived until the time of 'Abd al-Malik.
research_evidence: سندر مولى زنباع الجذامي. تقدم ذكره في زنباع. قال البخاريّ: سندر له صحبة

full: Wardan Clinet of Prophet (saw)
full_name_ar: وردان مولى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 9146) lists him as a client of the Prophet, included among the Companions by Abu Nu'aym. It cites a report via 'Ikrima from Ibn 'Abbas that Wardan fell from a palm tree and died, and the Prophet ordered that his inheritance be given to a man from his people.
research_evidence: وردان: مولى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم. ذكره أبو نعيم في الصّحابة
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full: Ma'bur al-Qibti (the Copt), al-Khasbi
full_name_ar: مأبور القبطي الخصبي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 7597) quotes al-Waqidi that al-Muqawqis sent Mariya and her sister Sirin to the Prophet along with gold, garments, the mule Duldul and the donkey 'Ufayr, accompanied by a eunuch called Ma'bur (also given as Habur). The report says the eunuch remained on his religion until he later accepted Islam during the Prophet's lifetime.
research_evidence: بعث المقوقس إلى رسول اللَّه صلّى اللَّه عليه وآله وسلم بمارية وأختها سيرين ... ومعهم خصيّ يقال له مأبور، ويقال هابور

full: Khadirah, Servent/client of Prophet(saw)
full_name_ar: خضرة خادم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ( رضي الله عنها
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 11101) lists Khadira as a servant of the Prophet, mentioned by Ibn Sa'd. Ibn Sa'd cites al-Waqidi's report from Salma Umm Rafi' that she, Khadira, Radwa and Maymuna bint Sa'd served the Prophet and that he freed them. Al-Baladhuri also mentioned her.
research_evidence: خضرة: خادم النبي صلّى اللَّه عليه وسلّم ذكرها ابن سعد، وأسند عن الواقديّ من حديث سلمى أم رافع
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full: Raqwa, Servent/client of Prophet(saw)
full_name_ar: رضوى مولاة رسول الله ( رضي الله عنها
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 11178) lists Radwa as a client (mawla) of the Prophet and refers back to the entry on Khadira, where Ibn Sa'd's report names her among the Prophet's female servants whom he freed. Abu Musa notes that al-Mustaghfiri mentioned her without further reports.
research_evidence: رضوى: مولاة رسول اللَّه صلّى اللَّه عليه وسلّم. تقدم ذكرها في الخاء المعجمة في خضرة، وقال أبو موسى: ذكرها المستغفري

full: Ruzaya, Servent of Prophet(saw), the client of Safiyya

bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 11176) describes Ruzayna as the client of Safiyya, wife of the Prophet, and also a servant of the Prophet. It quotes Abu 'Umar (Ibn 'Abd al-Barr) that her hadith on fasting 'Ashura' is transmitted among the people of Basra, with chains via 'Ulayla bint al-Kumayt from her mother Amina, recorded by Ibn Abi 'Asim, Ibn Manda and Abu Nu'aym.
research_evidence: رزينة: مولاة صفية زوج النبيّ صلّى اللَّه عليه وسلّم، وهي أيضا خادم رسول اللَّه صلّى اللَّه عليه وسلّم

full: Ghilan, Clinet of Prophet (saw)

bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 6943) lists him as a client of the Prophet and quotes Ibn al-Sakan that a single hadith is narrated from him, transmitted among the people of al-Raqqa. The chain given runs through Ja'far ibn Burqan and Dawud ibn 'Arad from Ghilan, with a hadith about the Dajjal.

full: Daws, Clinet of Prophet (saw)

bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 2412) lists him as a client of the Prophet, citing Ibn Manda that he is mentioned in a hadith (via Wahshi ibn Harb) in which the Prophet sent Daws to 'Uthman. full: Badham, Clinet of Prophet (saw)
full_name_ar: باذام مولى النبي صلى الله عليه وسل ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 582) lists Badham as a client (mawla) of the Prophet. It states that al-Baghawi mentioned him among the Prophet's clients and that Ibn 'Asakir followed him in this. No further details are given.
research_evidence: باذام مولى النّبي صلّى اللَّه عليه وسلم. ذكره البغويّ في موالي النبي صلّى اللَّه عليه وسلم، وتبعه ابن عساكر

full: Mawiya, the Client of Hujayr bin Abi Ihab

bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 11744, 'Mariya or Mawiya') notes that the narrators from Ibn Ishaq differed over her name, Yunus bin Bukayr and others giving it as Mawiya. Through Ibn Ishaq she relates that Khubayb bin 'Adi was imprisoned in her house in Mecca and that she once saw him holding a bunch of grapes. The page states that she accepted Islam and her Islam was good (وأسلمت وحسن إسلامها).
research_evidence: فحدثني عبد اللَّه بن أبي نجيح، عن مارية مولاة حجير بن أبي إهاب، قالت: حبس خبيب بمكّة في بيتي

full: Malik ibn Nuwayrah
full_name_ar: رضي الله عنه
bio: The English Wikipedia article describes him as chief of the Banu Yarbu', a clan of Banu Hanzala of Bani Tamim, whom the Prophet appointed to collect zakat from his tribe. It says he was accused of withholding zakat after the Prophet's death and was killed by Khalid ibn al-Walid during Abu Bakr's caliphate, in 632. The article cites accounts from Sayf ibn Umar, al-Tabari, Ibn Hajar and al-Dhahabi among others.

full: Umm Kabsha al-Quda'aiyya
full_name_ar: أم كبشة القضاعية ( رضي الله عنها
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 12219) lists Umm Kabsha al-Quda'iyya, a woman of Quda'a, and says Ibn Abi 'Asim mentioned her in al-Wuhdan, with her hadith recorded by Ibn Abi Shayba, Mutayyan, al-Tabarani and Ibn Sa'd. In it she asked the Prophet's permission to go out with an army to treat the wounded and give water, and he told her to stay back so that people would not say Muhammad campaigns with a woman. Ibn Hajar suggests this came after the conquest of Mecca. No death year is given.

It says she nursed Sa'd bin Mu'adh at the Battle of the Trench and took part in the Khaybar expedition, and quotes Ibn Hajar's Tahdhib al-Tahdhib calling her a woman of Aslam who treated the wounded. bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba lists him as a Qurashi of Banu Zuhra and maternal uncle of the Prophet. It cites reports about him from Ibn al-A'rabi's Mu'jam and Ibn Mandah, one of them transmitted by his son Wahb bin al-Aswad bin Wahb, which is the source of the reversed name form.
research_evidence: الأسود بن وهب بن عبد مناف بن زهرة القرشي الزهري، خال النبي صلّى اللَّه عليه وسلم

full_name_ar: الأسودبن زيدالأنصاري ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba lists him as an Ansari companion of the Khazraj (Banu Salima). It cites Musa bin Uqba, from Ibn Shihab, as naming him among those who were present at Badr. It also notes that his lineage is given differently in some transmissions.
research_evidence: الأسود بن زيد بن ثعلبة بن عبيد بن عدي بن غنم بن كعب بن سلمة بن سعد بن علي بن أسد بن ساردة الأنصاري الخزرجي

full_name_ar: الأسودوالدعامربن الأسود ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Abd al-Barr's al-Isti'ab (entry 51) lists al-Aswad as the father of Amir bin al-Aswad, per the transmission of Hushaym and Abu Awana from Ya'la bin Ata. The report says he was at the Prophet's Farewell Pilgrimage and saw the Prophet find two men at the Khayf mosque who had not prayed the dawn prayer. Ibn Abd al-Barr notes that Shu'ba instead names the narrator Jabir bin Yazid bin al-Aswad, from his father.
research_evidence: والد عامر بن الأسود، فيما روى هشيم وأبو عوانة عن يعلى ابن عطاء عن عامر بن الأسود عن أبيه

full_name_ar: الأسفع البكري ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn al-Athir's Usd al-Ghaba (entry 106) records al-Asfa' al-Bakri as transmitting a hadith about the greatest verse of the Quran. It notes that authorities disagree whether the companion is al-Asfa' himself or his son.

bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 217) lists al-Adbat al-Sulami and notes that Abu Nu'aym treated him as separate from the previous entry (al-Adbat bin Jini), while Ibn Hajar thinks they are the same man. It cites Abu Nu'aym and Ibn Mandah reporting, through Suhayl bin Suqayr, a hadith from him.

full: Amad bin Abad
full_name_ar: أمدبن أبدالحضرمي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 248) cites al-Tabarani's report that Mu'awiya had Amad bin Abad al-Hadrami brought to him, a man claiming to have lived about 300 years, who said he had seen the Prophet. Ibn Hajar says the chain appears broken and the story contains oddities. He notes Abu Hatim al-Sijistani gave another version in his book on the long-lived.

full: Amanaah bin Qays
full_name_ar: أماناة بن قيس بن الحارث بن شيبان بن الف ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 247) gives him as a Kindi and cites Ibn Sa'd, from Ibn al-Kalbi, that he came as a delegate to the Prophet. It reports that he lived 320 years, and that his son Yazid became Muslim, then apostatized and was killed in the caliphate of Abu Bakr.

bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 237) lists al-Aqmar al-Wadi'i of Hamdan, father of Ali and Kulthum, whose name is said to be Amr bin al-Harith bin Mu'awiya. It cites Ibn Shahin, who doubted his companionship, for a hadith through his son Ali that those who die of plague are martyrs, and notes Abu Musa also mentions him in his Dhayl.

full: An-Nuayman ibn Amr
full_name_ar: رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 8811) gives him as an Ansari of Banu al-Najjar. It cites Musa bin Uqba (from al-Zuhri) and Urwa as listing him among those at Badr, and Ibn Ishaq as saying he was at the last pledge of Aqaba. The entry, drawing on Ibn Sa'd, al-Zubayr bin Bakkar and others, records his well-known jokes, such as slaughtering a Bedouin's camel.

bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 236) says al-Aq'as bin Salama is counted among the people of al-Yamama and had companionship. It quotes Ibn Hibban that his name is also given as al-Uqaysir bin Salama al-Hanafi, and cites a report through al-Baghawi.

bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 68) gives his father's name variously as Jubayr, Hamza or Humayr. It cites Ibn Ishaq as naming him among those who emigrated to Abyssinia and Medina and were present at Badr, and cites Ibn Makula on the name.

bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 69) says Arbad bin Mukhshi had the kunya Abu Mukhshi and is better known by it. It gives Suwayd as another form of his name and refers to his fuller entry in the kunya section.

bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 70) lists Arbad as a servant of the Messenger of Allah, recorded by Ibn Mandah. Ibn Mandah's chain runs through Asbagh bin Zayd and Sa'id bin Abi Rashid to Zayd bin Ali bin al-Husayn, from his grandmother Fatima. Abu Musa later also recorded him.
research_evidence: ٧٠- أربد خادم رسول اللَّه صلى اللَّه عليه وسلم، ذكره ابن مندة

bio: Ibn al-Athir's Usd al-Ghaba (entry 97) says As'ad al-Khair settled in al-Sham and that al-Bukhari mentioned him in al-Wuhdan. It notes he may be the same as Abu Sa'd al-Khair, and that his real name may have been Ahmad.

full: Artat al tai
full_name_ar: أرطاة الطائي وقيل أبوأرطاة ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn al-Athir's Usd al-Ghaba (entry 67) says Artat al-Ta'i, also called Abu Artat, was sent by Jarir bin Abdullah to bring the Prophet the good news that the idol shrine of Dhu al-Khalasa had been destroyed, and the Prophet prostrated on hearing it. It notes that most transmitters name the messenger as Husayn bin Rabi'a instead. Ibn Mandah and Abu Nu'aym recorded him.

full_name_ar: أسعدبن عبدالله الخزاعي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn al-Athir's Usd al-Ghaba (entry 101) lists him as a companion of Khuza'a. It gives, via Abu Musa and Abu Nu'aym, his narration that the religion most beloved to Allah is the easy hanifiyya, transmitted through his descendants down to Sulayman bin Kathir al-Khuza'i.

bio: Ibn al-Athir's Usd al-Ghaba (entry 102) gives his lineage through Bali of Quda'a. It says he gave the pledge of al-Ridwan and took part in the conquest of Egypt, and that no narration is recorded from him.

full: As'ad bin Haritha bin Lauzaan
full_name_ar: أسعدبن حارثة بن لوذان الأنصاري الساعدي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn al-Athir's Usd al-Ghaba (entry 96) lists him as an Ansari of Banu Sa'ida, as given by Abu Nu'aym. It says he was martyred on the day of the Bridge (Yawm al-Jisr) in the caliphate of Umar bin al-Khattab, and that Abu Nu'aym and Abu Musa recorded him.

full_name_ar: أسعدبن سهل بن حنيف ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn al-Athir's Usd al-Ghaba (entry 100) says he was born in the Prophet's lifetime, two years before the Prophet's death, and was brought to him for blessing. The Prophet named him after his maternal grandfather As'ad bin Zurara and gave him that man's kunya. The entry counts him among the leading scholars.

bio: Ibn al-Athir's Usd al-Ghaba (entry 99) lists him as an Ansari of Banu Abd al-Ashhal who was martyred on the day of the Bridge (Yawm al-Jisr). It says Abu Nu'aym and Abu Musa recorded him, and that Ibn Mandah, Abu Nu'aym and Abu Umar also recorded him under the letter sin.

bio: Ibn al-Athir's Usd al-Ghaba (entry 103) lists him as an Ansari of Khazraj, Banu Sa'ida. It says he was killed as a martyr on the day of al-Yamama, and notes some confusion over whether he overlaps with another entry.
research_evidence: أسعد بْن يربوع الأنصاري الخزرجي الساعدي قتل يَوْم اليمامة شهيدًا

full: As'er
full_name_ar: أسعر‘وقيل ابن سعر‘وقيل سعر ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Entry 105 of Ibn al-Athir's Usd al-Ghaba fi Ma'rifat al-Sahaba: As'ar, also given as Ibn Sa'r or Sa'r. It relays, through Abu Murara al-Juhani from Ibn Sa'r from his father, a report that the Prophet's zakat collector refused a pregnant ewe and took only animals of the required ages. Ibn Manda listed him under As'ar, while Abu Nu'aym and Abu 'Umar listed him under Sa'r.
research_evidence: ١٠٥ - أسعر د: أسعر آخره راء، وقيل: ابن سعر، وقيل: سعر.

full: Asad bin akhi Kadija
full_name_ar: أسدبن أخي خديجة ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Entry 97 of Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba lists him under the heading Asad bin Khuwaylid, in the lineage of Khadija, quoting Abu 'Umar that Asad the nephew of Khadija narrated from the Prophet: 'Do not sell what you do not have.' His report was transmitted by Muhammad bin Jabir from Simak, and al-'Uqayli said its chain is questionable. Ibn Hajar notes that genealogists name only al-'Awwam and Nawfal as Khadija's brothers, and suggests he may be a son of Nawfal.
research_evidence: أسد ابن أخي خديجة روى عن النبي صلّى اللَّه عليه وسلم أنه قال: «لا تبع ما ليس عندك»
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full: Asad bin Haritha
full_name_ar: أسدبن حارثة العليمي الكلبي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Entry 99 of Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba: Asad bin Haritha al-Kalbi al-'Ulaymi, of Banu 'Ulaym bin Janab. Quoting Abu 'Umar (Ibn 'Abd al-Barr), it says he and his brother Qatan came to the Prophet with a group of their people and asked him to pray for rain for their land. No dates are given.
research_evidence: ٩٩- أسد بن حارثة الكلبي : ثم العليمي، من بني عليم بن جناب. قال أبو عمر: قدم

full: Asad bin Qarz
full_name_ar: أسدبن كرزبن عامر ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Entry 103 of Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba gives the lineage Asad bin Karz bin 'Amir bin 'Abdullah bin 'Abd Shams bin 'Uqba, and notes he was the grandfather of Khalid, the governor of Iraq. No dates are given.
research_evidence: ١٠٣- أسد بن كرز بن عامر بن عبد اللَّه بن عبد شمس بن عقبة

full: Asad bin Sa'ya
full_name_ar: أسدبن سعيةالقرظي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Entry 100 of Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba: Asad bin Sa'ya al-Qurazi, one of the Jews who accepted Islam. Citing Ibn Ishaq, Ibn al-Sakan, al-Tabari and Ibn Manda, it says he, Tha'laba bin Sa'ya and Asad bin 'Ubayd learned of the coming Prophet from Ibn al-Hayban, urged their people to follow him on the night before Qurayza fell, and then joined him. A report from Ibn 'Abbas links their conversion to Qur'an 3:113-114.

full: Asad bin Ubaid
full_name_ar: أسدبن عبيدالقرظي اليهودي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Entry 101 of Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba: Asad bin 'Ubayd al-Qurazi, listed by Ibn Hibban among the Companions. The preceding entry (Asad bin Sa'ya), citing Ibn Ishaq, names him with Tha'laba bin Sa'ya as Jews of Qurayza who accepted Islam and joined the Prophet on the night before Qurayza fell. No dates are given.

full: Asad bin Zrarah
full_name_ar: أسدبن زرارةالأنصاري ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Entry 92 of Ibn al-Athir's Usd al-Ghaba fi Ma'rifat al-Sahaba lists Asad bin Zurara al-Ansari, relaying through Abu Musa al-Madini a report, which al-Hakim called unusual in chain and text, about the Prophet's Night Journey and three qualities of 'Ali. Abu Musa comments that the name is really As'ad bin Zurara al-Ansari, and that no Companion is named Asad except Asad bin Khalid. The page gives no dates.

bio: Entry 209 of Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba: Asbagh bin Ghiyath, with the father's name also read as 'Attab. Ibn Manda relays through Jabir al-Ju'fi, whom Ibn Hajar calls weak, from al-Sha'bi from Asbagh a hadith beginning 'Your community has two traits that earlier nations did not have'. No dates are given.

full: Aseed bin abi Unaas
full_name_ar: أسيدبن أبي أناس بن زنيم الكناني الدؤلي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Entry 161 of Ibn al-Athir's Usd al-Ghaba fi Ma'rifat al-Sahaba: Asid bin Abi Unas bin Zunaym of Kinana (Banu al-Du'il). A poet who had satirised the Prophet, he was declared outlawed, and his people disowned him when seeking terms. After the conquest of Mecca he fled to al-Ta'if; Sariya bin Zunaym found him and brought him to the Prophet, where he accepted Islam, was granted safety, and recited verses in praise of the Prophet. Ibn Manda, Abu Nu'aym, Abu 'Umar and Abu Musa are cited.
research_evidence: ١٦١ - أسيد بن أبي أناس س: أسيد بالفتح أيضًا، وهو أسيد بْن أَبِي أناس بْن زنيم بْن عمرو بْن عَبْد

full: Aseed bin abi Usaid

bio: Entry 160 of Ibn al-Athir's Usd al-Ghaba fi Ma'rifat al-Sahaba: Asid bin Abi Usayd, of Banu Sa'ida of the Khazraj. 'Abdan al-Marwazi listed him among the Companions. He is linked to a report, through 'Umar bin al-Hakam, about the Prophet's marriage to a woman of Banu al-Jawn who sought refuge from him and was sent back to her family. Abu Musa comments on the differing attributions of the report.

full: Aa'yun bin Zuby'aah
full_name_ar: أعين بن ضبيعة بن ناجية بن عقال ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 222) gives his Tamimi Darimi lineage and calls him the nephew of Sa'sa'a ibn Najiya, grandfather of al-Farazdaq; it notes the author of al-Isti'ab listed him without evidence of companionship. He was the father of al-Nawar, wife of al-Farazdaq, fought with Ali at the Battle of the Camel and hamstrung the camel of Aisha. Ali sent him to Basra, where he was killed by treachery in the year 38 (فقتل أعين غيلة سنة ثمان وثلاثين).

bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (women's section, entry 11238) lists Zaynab, daughter of Abu Rafi' the freedman of the Prophet. famous: S'ad bin Salamh bin Wqsh al-'Ashhly
full: S'ad bin Salamh bin Wqsh al-'Ashhly
full_name_ar: سعد بن سلامة بن وقش الأشهلي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 3172) lists Sa'd ibn Salama ibn Waqsh al-Ashhali. Ibn al-Kalbi said he was martyred at the Battle of the Bridge (al-Jisr) with Abu Ubayd; it has also been said this is the name of Abu Na'ila.
research_evidence: سعد بن سلامة: بن وقش الأشهليّ. قال ابن الكلبي: استشهد يوم الجسر مع أبي عبيد وقد قيل: هو اسم أبي نائلة
dod_s: Died at: Battle of the Bridge — 13 AH / c. 634 CE (year of the event)

famous: S'ad bin 'Amr bin Thqf bin Malik
full: S'ad bin 'Amr bin Thqf bin Malik
full_name_ar: سعد بن عمرو بن ثقف بن مالك ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 3191) lists Sa'd ibn Amr ibn Thaqf of Banu al-Najjar of the Ansar. He is mentioned among those who fought at Uhud, and he was martyred at Bi'r Ma'una together with his son al-Tufayl and his nephew Sahl ibn Amir.
research_evidence: سعد بن عمرو: بن ثقف بن مالك بن مبذول بن النّجار الأنصاري. ذكروه فيمن شهد أحدا، واستشهد هو وابنه الطفيل
dod_s: Died at: Bi'r Ma'una — 4 AH / c. 625 CE (year of the event)

famous: Sa'da Aakhrh Ya'a Thtanyh W'awrd'h bin S
full: Sa'da Aakhrh Ya'a Thtanyh W'awrd'h bin Shahyn
full_name_ar: سعدى آخره ياء تحتانية وأورده بن شاهين ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 3252) lists Sa'di, whose name ends in the letter ya. Ibn Shahin included him and reported from Ibn Sa'd that he narrated from the Prophet about the camels of the zakat; Ibn Hajar says he could not settle the vocalisation of the name and thinks it is a nisba form.
research_evidence: سعدي: آخره ياء تحتانية. وأورده ابن شاهين، وحكى عن ابن سعد أن له رواية عن النّبي صلّى اللَّه عليه وسلم في إبل الصّدقة
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full: S'aid bin Ady al-Ansari
full_name_ar: سعيد بن عدي الأنصاري ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 3287) says al-Umawi listed him among those martyred at the Battle of al-Yamama, and Ibn Fathun added him. Ibn Hajar notes a similar entry under Sa'd ibn Uthman and says he does not know whether they were two brothers or one man whose name is disputed.
research_evidence: سعيد بن عديّ الأنصاريّ: ذكره الأمويّ فيمن استشهد يوم اليمامة. واستدركه ابن فتحون
dod_s: Died at: Battle of al-Yamama — 12 AH (some sources: 11 AH) / c. 633 CE (year of the event)

full: S'aid bin 'Amr al-Ydhy Balmhmlh Thm
full_name_ar: سعيد بن عمرو العيذي بالمهملة ثم ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 3293) lists Sa'id ibn Amr al-Aydhi al-Muharibi. Abu Ubayd mentioned him among those of his people who came to the Prophet in a delegation; al-Rushati notes that Abu Umar and Ibn Fathun did not mention him.
research_evidence: سعيد بن عمرو: العيذي- بالمهملة ثم التحتانية- المحاربيّ. ذكره أبو عبيد فيمن وفد على النبي صلّى اللَّه عليه وسلم من قومه
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full: S'yr bin Swad'h al-'Umary Wqyl
full_name_ar: سعير بن سوادة العامري وقيل ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 3310) lists Su'ayr ibn Sawada al-Amiri, also said to be named Sufyan. Ibn Manda reports via al-Ala' ibn al-Fadl from Abu Suwayd al-Minqari from his forefathers that Su'ayr ibn Sawada came to the Prophet.
research_evidence: سعير بن سوادة العامريّ: وقيل: هو سفيان. روى ابن مندة، من طريق العلاء بن الفضل، عن أبي سويد المنقري، عن آبائه
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

famous: Sufyan bin S'habh al-Mhry al-M'arwf Balk
full: Sufyan bin S'habh al-Mhry al-M'arwf Balkhrnq
full_name_ar: سفيان بن صهابة المهري المعروف بالخرنق ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 3325) lists Sufyan ibn Suhaba al-Mahri, the poet known as al-Kharnaq. Ibn Abi Dawud counted him among the companions, followed by Ibn Manda and others; Ibn Yunus noted that he witnessed the conquest of Egypt.
research_evidence: سفيان بن صهابة: المهري المعروف بالخرنق الشّاعر. ذكره ابن أبي داود في الصّحابة، وتبعه ابن مندة وغيره
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full: Salamh al-Dhry Yqal
full_name_ar: سلامة العذري يقال ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 3358) lists Salama al-Udhri, also called al-Muhallab. It says Ali ibn Harb mentioned in a book of his that he came to the Prophet in a delegation, as reported by al-Rushati.
research_evidence: سلامة العذري: يقال له المهلب، ذكره علي بن حرب العراقي في كتاب البحار له أنه وفد على النبي صلّى اللَّه عليه وسلم
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

famous: Slma bin al-Qyn bin 'Amr bin Bakr
full: Slma bin al-Qyn bin 'Amr bin Bakr
full_name_ar: سلمى بن القين بن عمرو بن بكر ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 3426) lists Sulma ibn al-Qayn al-Tamimi al-Hanzali. Ibn al-Kalbi said he was a companion, and he is also mentioned in the entry on Harmala ibn Murayta.
research_evidence: سلمى بن القين: بن عمرو بن بكر بن مالك بن حنظلة بن مالك بن زيد مناة التميمي الحنظليّ. قال ابن الكلبيّ: له صحبة
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full: Snan bin Suwayd al-Jhny
full_name_ar: سنان بن سويد الجهني ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 3515) lists Sinan ibn Suwayd al-Juhani. Ibn al-Sakan reported via Abd Allah ibn Dawud ibn al-Dilhath al-Juhani that Yasir, Sinan and Sayyar, sons of Suwayd, were brothers who all met the Prophet.
research_evidence: سنان بن سويد الجهنيّ: روى ابن السكن من طريق عبد اللَّه بن داود بن الدّلهاث الجهنيّ، قال: كان ياسر بن سويد، وسنان بن سويد، وسيار بن سويد، كلهم إخوة
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full: Snan bin Zuhyr al-'Asady
full_name_ar: سنان بن ظهير الأسدي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 3518) lists Sinan ibn Zuhayr al-Asadi. Abu Umar (Ibn Abd al-Barr) said he was a companion, and Abu Nu'aym reported via Uqba ibn Jawdan from his father that Sinan said he gave the Prophet a she-camel as a gift.
research_evidence: سنان بن ظهير الأسدي: قال أبو عمر: له صحبة. وروى أبو نعيم من طريق عقبة بن جودان، عن أبيه، عن سنان بن ظهير
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

famous: Swa'a bin al-Harith bin Zalm bin Hdad
full: Swa'a bin al-Harith bin Zalm bin Hdad
full_name_ar: سواء بن الحارث بن ظالم بن حداد ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 3591) lists Sawa' ibn al-Harith ibn Zalim ibn Haddad of Muharib ibn Khasafa, brother of Asim, and says his story comes in Asim's entry. Ibn Hajar raises the question of whether he is the same man as Sawa' ibn al-Harith al-Muharibi in the preceding entry or a different person.
research_evidence: سواء بن الحارث بن ظالم: بن حداد بن ذهل بن طريف بن محارب بن خصفة، أخو عاصم. سيأتي خبره في ترجمة
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

bio: Entry 3710 in the third section (mukhadramun, those who lived in the Prophet's era without meeting him) of Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba. It says he was of Tayy then Sinbis, took part in the conquest of Iraq, and drowned in the Tigris on the day the Muslims crossed to al-Mada'in, the only one to drown. Ibn Hajar cites Ibn al-Kalbi.
research_evidence: سليل بن زيد: بن مالك بن المعلّى الطّائي ثم السّنبسيّ. له إدراك، وشهد فتوح العراق
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)
